Text: {D(AdminHead)} is always boasting about {his(AdminHead)} prized possession: a physical book

“Tales of long-eared men and bearded children will not help with our current affairs,” you grumble. “They’re not children! And they would help, if-” {His(AdminHead)} face reddens. “That’s not why I’m here. Look at the imprint.” Stamped on the flyleaf are coordinates within {StarSystem}. You laugh. “You think this library still exists? Even if it did, it would’ve been raided decades ago!” {D(AdminHead)}’s face is now a mortified purple. You sigh. “Why not? But don’t expect an adventure like in your beloved book.”
Persuaded you to visit an ancient library
You land on a barren lakeside hill; no signs of colonisation

Sulking, {d(AdminHead)} picks up a rock and skips it across the lake. Plop... plop... plop... Dong! Bewildered, you stare at the lake, then at {d(AdminHead)}, then back at the lake. “Fetch the drone!” you cry. You hurry the drone to the point of impact and discover a tiny pole sticking out of the water. You send the drone below the surface. {D(AdminHead)} gasps. A whole installation lies beneath the lake. The pole is the tip of its largest building: the library citadel. “Suit up,” you grin. “You wanted an adventure, did you not?”
Drone scans show an entrance to the library from the lakebed

You ignore security’s pleas to explore ahead of you, and dive into the water. {D(AdminHead)} reluctantly follows. You marvel at the refracted light: at this depth it dances across submerged domes, scattering through archways until it fades into the depths. “Switch to night vision,” you radio: your torchlight is all but snuffed out in the watery darkness. Finally, you reach the security entrance. “{TechHead} ran the numbers,” you explain. “As long as we’re exactly 10 meters from the doorway when we override the lock, the current should flush us into the building in one piece,” you say. “I beg your pardon?!” {d(AdminHead)} exclaims.
“That was the stupidest thing I’ve done in my entire life!” gasps {d(AdminHead)}

Rising from the wet marble floor, you look around - and gasp. Bookshelves the size of buildings soar into the sky - or rather, a ceiling painted with clouds and winged humans. 

Statues to your left and right flank a large staircase. At the first landing, it splits in two directions. You study the floor plan.

“That hangar could be our way out,” you say to {d(AdminHead)}. No answer. Glancing back you see {him(AdminHead)} turning in circles, open-mouthed and wide-eyed.

You turn back to the map.

As you traverse another breathtaking hall, a crash reverberates through the floor

Your stunt must have damaged the entrance doors; the building is flooding! “Grab as much as you can!” you bark. “We make for the hangar!”

As you run past the staircase, you see the water rising towards you. But you reach the hangar and cheer: a handful of ships are still docked.

“How are we supposed to leave?” {d(AdminHead)} shouts as you strap in. “If we open the hangar roof, the water will flatten us!”

“We hold tight and wait,” you reply.

“Are you serious?!” {d(AdminHead)} cries.
Scared for {his(AdminHead)} life
The incoming torrent almost rips the tethers from the ground

The water rises above the windows, the shuttle swaying in the torrent. Your heart hammers against your chest.

Once the water reaches the ceiling, you open the hangar roof. For a second, the sunlight reminds you of the library’s paradisal frescoes.

“Hold on!” you shout, and launch the shuttle.

The shuttle rises, slowly: first out of the lake, then into space. “Not bad, eh?” you shrug, with a self-satisfied smirk.

“I think... I will stick to my books from now on,” {he(AdminHead)} murmurs, face pale as snow.

“At least now you’ve got more than one to choose from,” you grin.
